descripcion_geo: City founded by Attalus II of Pergamon on the border between Lydia and Phrygia, on the edge of the plateau.
importancia_estrategica: Gate of the Phrygian plateau; city ​​of frequent earthquakes.

historias.titulo: Letter to the church of Philadelphia
historias.descripcion: Christ congratulates the church of Philadelphia without reproach; He promises an open door.

historias.titulo: The door that no one can close
historias.descripcion: Christ has the key to David and opens doors; It promises to make adversaries prostrate.
Christ promises to save the faithful of Philadelphia in the hour of universal testing.

personajes.descripcion: It conveys the only blameless message of the glorious Christ to Philadelphia.
He founded the city and gave it his name ('brotherly love').
He wrote a letter to the Philadelphia church while being transferred to Rome.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Missionary city at the Phrygian gate; his church received the blameless praise of the Apocalypse.

cristianismo.descripcion: Christ promises Philadelphia an 'open door' that no one can close, a symbol of missionary opportunity and divine protection.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Christ promises Philadelphia an 'open door' that no one can close, a symbol of missionary opportunity and divine protection.
